data.narrative:
Natilus is a Series A autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $16M to date. The peer universe in this sector consists of 8 private companies—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—with no public comparables available for direct valuation anchoring.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method was the primary applicable approach. This method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $16M total raised as a proxy baseline, implying a post-Series A valuation of $32M. The peer-median approach was not viable; while 7 same-sector companies exist, no subset of 3 or more matched concurrent stage, proximity, or valuation tier criteria simultaneously, making a median-based comparison unreliable without risking distortion from heterogeneous peer characteristics.

The triangulation yields a range of $27M (low) to $37M (high), centered on $32M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single method and underscores the primary uncertainty: absence of sufficiently granular comparable transaction data at this stage within autonomous systems. Further valuation refinement would require either evidence of company-specific revenue, burn rate, or runway relative to sector peers, or expansion of the comparable set to adjacent subsectors. The $32M median should be treated as indicative pending additional financial or operational metrics.
